key_insight: A marker-less, mobile multi-camera capture system enables accurate 3D reconstruction of hands and manipulated objects in unconstrained, in-the-wild egocentric scenarios, producing diverse data that helps models generalize beyond studio conditions.
problem_solved: Existing hand–object interaction datasets are mostly collected in controlled studio setups, limiting environmental diversity and causing trained models to struggle on real-world, egocentric manipulation tasks.
method: Marker-less, nearly unconstrained wearable/multi-camera rig for egocentric capture with synchronized views and calibration.
Multi-view 3D reconstruction and pose estimation pipeline to recover detailed hand and object geometry without markers.
Scaleable annotation and dataset assembly across diverse real-world environments to create ground-truth for training and evaluation.
impact: Provides realistic, diverse training data and ground truth for 3D hand-object understanding, improving robustness of models used in AR/VR, robotics, assistive tech, and egocentric perception research.
visual_elements: Illustration of the wearable/multi-camera capture rig and capture setup
Side-by-side comparison: studio-captured vs in-the-wild examples highlighting increased diversity
Multi-view image montage with overlayed 3D reconstructions of hand + object
Pipeline flowchart: capture → multi-view reconstruction → 3D annotation → dataset/model training
paper_title: SHOW3D: Capturing Scenes of 3D Hands and Objects in the Wild
paper_authors: Patrick Rim, Kevin Harris, Braden Copple, Shangchen Han, Xu Xie
